content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"Claims 1, 2, 3 and 12 can be traced from cited evidence (S1 testimony, Privacy Investigation Report, coworker interviews) to the Agency's findings, but claims 4-11, 13 and 14 have no visible findings, and the harassment conclusion rests on general statements like 'even accepting allegations as true'."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations are attributed (Privacy Investigation Report, S1, Witness 1 and 2, the July 1, 2019 letter), but the discipline letters have unidentified addressees, a coworker name is blank in the privacy letter, 'undisputed evidence' on the 8-hour tour is uncited, and the Agency's claim that coworkers confirmed no disclosure is not tied to specific interviews."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Key dates are given (April 8-9, 2019 privacy request, June 26, 2018 surgery, July 1, 2019 letter, September 4-5, 2019 discipline), but claim 1 shifts between May 2018 and Nov/Dec 2017, claim 14 has no dates, and the sequence of the privacy investigation and the formal complaint steps is not laid out."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The record shows the Agency adopted ORM's partial dismissal and analyzed claims under a disparate treatment theory with credibility reasoning, but it does not name the final decision-maker, and the treatment of Witness 13, the discrepancy between the three coworkers in the July 1 letter and the two in the report, and the unaddressed claims is not explained."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"The record cannot stand alone for an independent merits assessment because several accepted claims were never resolved, the privacy letter conflicts with the investigation report, key witness statements are only paraphrased, and the discipline documents are unattributed."}}}
